# pulumi/pulumi-python

**Pulumi IaC: infrastructure as code in any programming language.**

[Pulumi IaC](https://www.pulumi.com/product/infrastructure-as-code/) is an open-source infrastructure as code tool for creating, deploying, and managing cloud infrastructure on any cloud. Write your infrastructure in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, C#, Java, or YAML, and use the loops, functions, classes, testing tools, and package managers you already know.

## About this image

A slim image that contains the Pulumi CLI and Python, for running Pulumi programs written in Python.

It contains:

- The Pulumi CLI and the Python language runtime.
- Python, with pip, [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/), and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
- `git` and `curl`.

## Python versions

`pulumi/pulumi-python` ships Python 3.13. To use a different version of Python, use the image for that version instead:

| Image | Python version |
| --- | --- |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python` | Python 3.13 |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python-3.10` | Python 3.10 |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python-3.11` | Python 3.11 |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python-3.12` | Python 3.12 |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python-3.13` | Python 3.13 (default) |
| `pulumi/pulumi-python-3.14` | Python 3.14 |

The versions on offer follow the supported releases of Python. When the default changes, `pulumi/pulumi-python` moves to the new version, so pin an image with a version in its name if you need to stay on a specific one.

## Tags and platforms

Each Pulumi release is published under these tags, where `<version>` is the Pulumi CLI version, for example `3.200.0`:

| Tag | Base image | Platforms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<version>`, `latest` | Debian 13 (trixie) slim | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-debian` | Debian 13 (trixie) slim | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-debian-amd64` | Debian 13 (trixie) slim | `linux/amd64` |
| `<version>-debian-arm64` | Debian 13 (trixie) slim | `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-ubi` | [Red Hat UBI 9 minimal](https://hub.docker.com/r/redhat/ubi9-minimal) | `linux/amd64` |

Tags without a suffix are the same image as the `-debian` tag. The `-debian` tag is a multi-platform manifest list, so `docker pull` selects the right image for your machine. UBI images use [`microdnf`](https://github.com/rpm-software-management/microdnf) as their package manager.

## Usage

Mount your Pulumi project into the container and run Pulumi commands against it:

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN \
  -v "$(pwd)":/pulumi/projects \
  -w /pulumi/projects \
  pulumi/pulumi-python \
  pulumi preview
```

Pass the credentials for your cloud provider as environment variables, too. This image contains only the Pulumi CLI and the tools listed above. If your program needs other tools, such as `helm` for the Kubernetes provider, use this image as the base for your own image and install them there. The [`pulumi/pulumi`](https://hub.docker.com/r/pulumi/pulumi) image includes many common tools.

## Releases

Images are built and published automatically for every release of the [Pulumi CLI](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/releases), usually once a week, with patch releases in between when needed. Image tags match the version of the Pulumi CLI they contain. For example, when Pulumi `v3.200.0` is released, it's published as `3.200.0`. The `latest` tag always points to the most recent release.

To avoid unexpected upgrades, pin your image to a specific version tag rather than `latest`.

Images are scanned nightly for vulnerabilities. We remediate findings where we can, on a best-effort basis. Some findings, such as vulnerabilities in base images with no available fix, are outside our control.

## Getting help

- Problems with an image, such as a missing tool, a vulnerability, or a broken tag: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers/issues/new).
- Problems with the Pulumi CLI or SDKs: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/new/choose).
- Questions: ask in the [Pulumi Community Slack](https://slack.pulumi.com/).
